summary: The Federal Communications Commission has authorized SpaceX to deploy up to one million satellites for space-based data centers, a regulatory approval that has drawn skepticism from scientists concerned about orbital congestion. In international launch activities, China launched the Shenzhou 24 mission carrying three crew members, marking the arrival of the first Pakistani astronaut aboard the Tiangong space station, while Rocket Lab launched a Japanese satellite on Thanksgiving Day. In planetary exploration and astronomy, the European Space Agency’s Hera spacecraft returned its first close-up images of the impact crater created on the asteroid Dimorphos by NASA’s DART mission, NASA’s Europa Clipper executed an Earth flyby en route to Jupiter, and astronomers utilizing the James Webb Space Telescope discovered the most distant supermassive black hole-powered quasar observed to date, formed just 630 million years after the Big Bang. In defense developments, the U.S. Air Force awarded Boeing a $2.8 billion contract for additional KC-46 tankers, the Pentagon elevated an artificial intelligence program used for classification decisions, and the U.S. Army fully fielded its first Dark Eagle hypersonic battery while the Department of Defense requested congressional stopgap funding for its MQ-9 fleet and Golden Dome initiative under a continuing resolution. On the commercial front, private equity firm Cerberus agreed to acquire Airbus U.S. Space & Defense, and geospatial intelligence firm BlackSky acquired data science company EpochGeo. Looking ahead, industry observers should monitor progress on Japan's newly unveiled rover prototype designed to prospect for water ice on future lunar missions.
